MENTOR: Good choice. Tile, Caption and Stamp are now your group.

That's the comp at 0 s. The frame came back too small for me to make out where the three layers sit, so I won't describe positions from it.

Here's the idea. A parent carries its children's **position, scale and rotation**, and each child still runs its own animation on top. Your comp already has an example: Hatch follows Hatch Rig. You'll do the same thing here. Add one invisible handle, a null, put it where the group should turn or scale from, attach Tile, Caption and Stamp to it, then animate only the null.

Two things to keep in mind:
- Children inherit position, scale and rotation, **but not opacity or effects**.
- A null **never shows in the render**, so it adds nothing to how the group looks.

Your turn: add a null with **Layer > New > Null Object**. Then tell me: **where should the group turn or scale from?** It could be a corner, the middle of an edge, or the middle of the group. "It'll only slide" is a fine answer too.

### Turn 3: the project is an open comp
LEARNER: I added a null and put it in the middle of the group, since the group turns from there. Done.

MENTOR: Null 1 is in the right place: its pivot sits in the middle of Tile, Caption and Stamp, so the group will turn around its center. One thing worth knowing: a null's pivot is the top-left corner of its square, so that's the corner to line up with the spot.

Next, attach the group to it. In the timeline, use the **pick whip in the Parent column** to parent Tile, Caption and Stamp to Null 1. You can drag it from each layer onto Null 1, or pick Null 1 from the column's menu. If you can't see that column, right-click any column heading and choose **Columns > Parent & Link**.

Do it with no key held. Say "done" when all three are parented. If you'd like, I can parent Tile first so you can see how it works, and you do the other two.

MENTOR: You passed on the first try. Tile, Caption and Stamp all follow Null 1, and none of them moved when you parented them. Their own keys are still there, so each layer keeps its own animation and slides with the group on top of that. The null's slide is on its Position, which is where a group move belongs.

A few notes on the result:
- The group starts and stops hard. You can soften Null 1's keys with the easing you learned earlier if you want it gentler.
- It's worth renaming Null 1 after what it moves, something like "Tile Rig".
- You put the null at the group's center because the group turns from there, so try keying Null 1's Rotation next to watch all three turn around that point.

I've noted all this for next time.
